cb-01: `(*Command).ExecuteC` is defined in `command.go:1052` and returns `(*Command, error)`. The shown code supplies a background context if needed, delegates child calls to the root, runs the optional pre-execution hook, initializes help and completion commands, checks command groups, selects explicit or process arguments, and resolves the command with `Traverse` or `Find` (`command.go:1052–1093`). `Execute` discards its command return and returns the error (`command.go:1038–1041`); `ExecuteContextC` sets the context before calling it (`command.go:1046–1049`). The rest of ExecuteC is not shown.
cb-02: `(*Command).MarkFlagsMutuallyExclusive(flagNames ...string)` is in `flag_groups.go:65–77`. It merges persistent flags, looks up each named flag, and appends the space-joined group names to that flag's `mutuallyExclusive` annotation. A missing flag or annotation error causes a panic. Appending permits a flag to belong to multiple groups. `ValidateFlagGroups` collects those annotations into `mutuallyExclusiveGroupStatus` (`flag_groups.go:81–96`); the actual exclusivity check is outside the shown excerpt.
cb-03: `GenMarkdownTree(cmd *cobra.Command, dir string) error` is in `doc/md_docs.go:125–129`. It calls `GenMarkdownTreeCustom` with an empty file prepender and an identity link handler. The custom function recursively processes available child commands except additional help topics, then creates a file whose basename is the command path with spaces replaced by underscores plus `markdownExtension`, writes the prepender, and calls `GenMarkdownCustom`; errors are returned (`doc/md_docs.go:133–158`).
cb-04: `(*Command).RegisterFlagCompletionFunc` in `completions.go:133–146` registers a callback of type `func(cmd *Command, args []string, toComplete string) ([]string, ShellCompDirective)` for a named flag. It rejects nonexistent flags and duplicate registrations, locks `flagCompletionMutex`, and stores the callback in `flagCompletionFunctions[flag]`. `GetFlagCompletionFunc` retrieves it under a read lock (`completions.go:148–160`). The comment in `shell_completions.go:52–53` recommends this Go callback API for completion across all shells.
cb-07: `flag_groups.go` contains flag-group validation helpers. `ValidateFlagGroups` skips validation when flag parsing is disabled and collects required-together, one-required, and mutually-exclusive annotation groups (`flag_groups.go:81–99`). `processFlagForGroupAnnotation` ignores a group unless all its flags exist, using `hasAllFlags` (`flag_groups.go:121–134`, `111–119`). `validateRequiredFlagGroups` accepts all flags set or all unset, but returns a deterministically sorted missing-flags error for a partially set group (`flag_groups.go:144–165`).
cb-08: `doc/man_docs.go` provides man-page generation: `GenMan(cmd *cobra.Command, header *GenManHeader, w io.Writer) error` writes a command's man page and allows a nil header (`doc/man_docs.go:103–106`); `GenManTreeOptions` includes `Header` and `Path` (`82–86`). `fillHeader` defaults the title to the uppercase command name with spaces escaped as `\-`, the section to `1`, and the date to the current time or parsed `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH`. It formats the date as `Jan 2006`, rejects an invalid epoch, and supplies the auto-generation source when enabled (`118–141`).
cb-09: `shell_completions.go` is in package `cobra` and imports `pflag` (`shell_completions.go:15–19`). It provides helpers for required flags and filename completion: `Command.MarkFlagRequired` delegates to the flag-set helper and is documented to prioritize completion and reject invocation without the flag (`21–26`); `MarkFlagFilename` restricts completion by extension (`42–43`); `MarkPersistentFlagFilename` applies that helper to `c.PersistentFlags()` (`58–62`).
cb-11: Required flags are checked by `(*Command).ValidateRequiredFlags` in `command.go:1147–1168`. It visits `c.Flags()`, finds flags annotated with `BashCompOneRequiredFlag`, and collects those whose annotation is `"true"` and whose `Changed` field is false; it then returns `required flag(s) "..." not set`. It returns nil when `DisableFlagParsing` is enabled. The supplied excerpt identifies the validator but does not show its call site in command execution.

cb-13: `SuggestionsFor` scans available child commands and adds a command name when `ld(typedName, cmd.Name(), true)` is at most `SuggestionsMinimumDistance` or the command name has the typed name as a case-insensitive prefix; a case-insensitive match in the child's `SuggestFor` list also adds its name (`command.go:832–850`). `findSuggestions` returns nothing when `DisableSuggestions` is true, defaults a nonpositive distance to 2, and formats matches under `Did you mean this?` (`command.go:750–762`).
cb-14: Shell completion scripts request results through the hidden command represented by `ShellCompRequestCmd`, or `ShellCompNoDescRequestCmd` for results without descriptions (`completions.go:27–31`). Its `Run` handler dispatches the supplied arguments to `cmd.getCompletions(args)`, receiving the final command, completions, directive, and error (`completions.go:202–206`). Errors are reported with `CompErrorln`, but processing continues so valid completions and the directive can still be emitted; `CalledAs()` determines whether the no-description command was used (`207–215`).

The comment on `updateParentsPflags` says it collects new persistent flags from all parents and initializes the parent flag set when needed (`1855–1863`). `LocalFlags()` triggers this merge (`1669–1671`). For each child, `AddCommand` rejects the parent itself, sets `cmds[i].parent = c`, updates the parent's maximum usage/path/name lengths, applies any global normalization function to the child, appends the child to `c.commands`, and marks the command list unsorted (`command.go:1302–1329`).
cb-22: The shown man-page generator uses recursive depth-first traversal: `GenManTreeFromOpts` iterates `cmd.Commands()`, skips unavailable commands and additional help topic commands, and recursively calls itself on each remaining child with the same options, returning immediately on error (`doc/man_docs.go:48–60`). It resumes the current command's page setup after the child loop (`61–69`). The response also shows Markdown and YAML tree generators beginning with `cmd.Commands()` loops (`doc/md_docs.go:133–134`, `doc/yaml_docs.go:60–61`), but their traversal bodies are omitted.

Command lookup first accepts an exact name or alias; otherwise, when prefix matching is enabled, it collects commands satisfying `hasNameOrAliasPrefix(next)` and returns a match only if exactly one command qualifies (`command.go:770–785`).

ci-1222:
For flag completion, write a Go callback with this signature and register it on the command:

```go
func completeFlag(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string, toComplete string) ([]string, cobra.ShellCompDirective)
```

Call `cmd.RegisterFlagCompletionFunc("flag-name", completeFlag)` after the flag exists, and handle its returned error. The callback returns completion strings and a shell directive; registration rejects nonexistent flags and duplicate registrations (`completions.go:132–146`). The response supplies the registration contract but does not define the individual directive values.

Thus it exposes the recorded invocation name for a command marked as called; the provided excerpt does not show where that called state is set.
ci-1358: After defining the flags, call `cmd.MarkFlagsMutuallyExclusive("flag-a", "flag-b")`, using the flag names. `MarkFlagsMutuallyExclusive` merges persistent flags, looks up each name, and annotates each member with the space-joined group; it panics if a flag is missing (`flag_groups.go:65–77`). Flags can belong to multiple groups because annotations are appended. `ValidateFlagGroups` is documented to enforce these groups (`79–80`), and completion hides the other group members when one is present (`223–224`).
